indicators.label: Resting heart rate
indicators.whyItMatters: Cardiovascular deconditioning, stress, dehydration, and arrhythmia all show up in resting heart rate.
howToMeasure: Sit quietly for a few minutes before measuring.
Use a wrist/chest sensor, or count your pulse for 30 seconds and double it.

green: Heart rate is in the normal range.
red: Sit down, rest, and contact the flight surgeon.
critical: Stop activity, sit or secure yourself, and contact the flight surgeon now.

indicators.source: General adult clinical reference (starting default, not a validated space-medicine limit) — see SPEC §3.2

indicators.label: Blood pressure (systolic)
indicators.whyItMatters: Fluid shift in micro-g changes blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.
howToMeasure: Use an automatic cuff, seated and relaxed.

green: Blood pressure is in the normal range.
red: Sit/rest and contact the flight surgeon.

indicators.label: Fasting blood glucose
indicators.whyItMatters: Insulin resistance and nutrition changes in space show up in fasting glucose.
howToMeasure: Use a finger-prick glucometer while fasting.

green: Glucose is in the normal range.
yellow: Re-check your diet and hydration; re-measure later.

indicators.label: Body temperature
indicators.whyItMatters: Infection and immune changes, and heat management in a closed habitat.
howToMeasure: Use an ear, forehead, or oral thermometer.

green: Temperature is in the normal range.
yellow: Rest and re-measure in a couple of hours.
red: Isolate, hydrate, and contact the flight surgeon.

indicators.label: Blood oxygen (SpO2)
indicators.whyItMatters: Cabin air quality, CO2 build-up, and habitat pressure all affect SpO2.
howToMeasure: Use a pulse oximeter on a fingertip.

green: SpO2 is in the normal range.
red: Sit down, check cabin/suit O2, alert crew, contact the flight surgeon.
critical: Sit down, alert crew, and contact the flight surgeon now.

indicators.label: Sleep duration
indicators.whyItMatters: Isolation and circadian disruption are strongly linked to sleep, mood, and performance.
howToMeasure: Log the hours you actually slept, from a sleep diary or wearable.

green: Sleep duration is in the normal range.
yellow: Try to protect your sleep window tonight.
red: Talk to a crewmate or the flight surgeon about your sleep.

indicators.label: Mood
indicators.whyItMatters: Behavioural health and isolation effects show up first in day-to-day mood.
howToMeasure: Rate your mood on the 1-5 emoji scale.

green: Mood is in the normal range.
yellow: Consider talking to a crewmate today.
red: Talk to a crewmate and consider a private call with the flight surgeon/counsellor.
critical: Talk to a crewmate now and contact the flight surgeon/counsellor.

indicators.label: Exercise (resistance + cardio)
indicators.whyItMatters: Bone and muscle protection depend on daily resistance and cardio exercise.
howToMeasure: Log total minutes of resistance and cardio exercise for the day.

yellow: Try to fit in more exercise today.
red: Bone and muscle protection is at risk — prioritise exercise.

howToMeasure: Log the daily reading from your personal dosimeter, if available.

yellow: Approaching the radiation budget — review shelter/storm procedures.
red: Over the radiation budget — contact the flight surgeon.
